account:
It is ten in the morning, time for my scheduled market walk in the plaza. So far I have been at the town hall speaking with the secretary and builder. The builder wants a paid commission for this week's repairs and has lanterns and planks ready. I asked for an inspection of public roads, the bridge and lamps, followed by an itemized estimate before any paid work. I have not approved a price or construction. The secretary says there is no repair list or approved budget. This seems to be ordinary town maintenance planning, not evidence of a particular hazard.

The appointment arrangements are somewhat confused. The secretary initially reported the appointments chest empty after I had taken the book to read it; I returned it and saw the secretary retrieve it. There is no reason to regard that as suspicious. More importantly, the book schedules tea at three with a neighbour in a dockside cottage on the east bank but gives neither a host's name nor a precise cottage. I do not remember the host. The secretary offered to confirm the address and asked the builder whether he knew. No correspondence has arrived this morning.

My latest attempt to explain that I did not recall the host and to request a bridge inspection was not heard by anyone, so I cannot assume either person received those instructions. Both have now left my sight. Three townsfolk are visible near the town hall road point; I have not observed what they are doing. I have noticed no definite emergency or unusual activity beyond the incomplete tea arrangements and the unresolved repair commission.
